title: Union political money against the pay of the units it represents
question: Did the unions whose committees gave most in San Francisco politics see faster growth in overtime, pay or scale for their units, fiscal 2019 to 2026?
finding: Per person represented, the largest givers were Firefighters Local 798 ($3.5 million since 2015, 1,800 dollars per person paid in fiscal 2026; overtime 1.73 times 2019, pay per person 1.46 times, median top of scale 25.1% higher); Deputy Sheriffs’ Association ($1.2 million since 2015, 1,595 dollars per person paid in fiscal 2026; overtime 1.87 times 2019, pay per person 1.48 times, median top of scale 31.2% higher); Police Officers Association ($3.1 million since 2015, 1,371 dollars per person paid in fiscal 2026; overtime 2.57 times 2019, pay per person 1.74 times, median top of scale 26.4% higher). Across 11 union families the rank correlation of giving per person with overtime growth is 0.727, with the level of overtime (share of regular pay) 0.65, with pay growth per person 0.364 and with scale growth -0.205 (11 families): the scale rose by about the same for nearly every unit, while overtime and premiums did not. That is a description of 11 union families, not a test of cause.
how: Giving is the “unions” results as published on this site: contributions and independent spending by committees carrying each union's name, 2015 onward. Each payroll unit is put in a union family with the same name patterns the “unions” analysis uses; 'POA' is bridged to the Police Officers Association because a City document spells it out (“San Francisco Police Officers Association (POA)”). Pay growth is total salary per person paid; scale growth is the median change in the top biweekly rate of the unit's job codes, FY2018-19 to FY2025-26 (DHR tables); 'next year' is FY2025-26 to FY2026-27 from the two hourly-rates workbooks. Families with fewer than 200 people paid by the City are left out, because a per-person figure for a small unit is dominated by giving about members who work elsewhere. Rank correlation is Spearman's.
limits: Political giving and bargaining are permitted; labor agreements are negotiated by the Department of Human Resources and adopted by ordinance, and many uniformed raises are set by a Charter formula or arbitration, not by a vote. Union families' giving includes measures outside San Francisco and union-wide committees. Overtime follows vacancies. A handful of unions cannot show cause; timing is a question, not proof.
